title: Countable DG submodule representing countable cohomology
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(A,d_A)$ be an associative unital $\mathbf Z$-graded ring with $d_A:A^i\to A^{i+1}$, $d_A^2=0$, and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d_A(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module means a graded right $A$-module $M$ with $d_M:M^j\to M^{j+1}$, $d_M^2=0$, and $d_M(ma)=d_M(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d_A(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Cohomology is $H^i(M)=\ker(d_M:M^i\to M^{i+1})/\operatorname{im}(d_M:M^{i-1}\to M^i)$; a quasi-isomorphism is a DG module map inducing isomorphisms on all these groups. Countable means countable in the sense of [def-sfb-countable-set]. Assume the set $\coprod_i A^i$ is countable. Let $N$ be a right differential graded $A$-module such that every $H^i(N)$ is countable. There exists a graded right $A$-submodule $M\subseteq N$, stable under $d_N$, such that $\coprod_i M^i$ is countable and the inclusion $M\hookrightarrow N$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: Use the injection-into-$\mathbf N$ definition [def-sfb-countable-set]. Subsets of a countable set are countable by restricting its injection; the image of any map from a countable set is countable by assigning each image element the least code of a preimage. A product of two countable sets is countable: compose their injections with $(a,b)\mapsto 2^a(2b+1)$, whose injectivity follows by removing the maximal power of $2$. The degree set $\mathbf Z$ is countable via $i\mapsto 2i$ for $i\geq0$ and $i\mapsto-2i-1$ for $i<0$. These explicit coding observations will be used below.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: For a set $T\subseteq\coprod_i N^i$ of homogeneous elements, put $U=T\cup d_N(T)$, with degrees retained, and define $G(T)^k$ to consist of all finite sums $\sum_{\ell}u_\ell a_\ell$ with $u_\ell\in U$, homogeneous $a_\ell\in A$, and $|u_\ell|+|a_\ell|=k$. Include the empty sum $0\in N^k$. Addition concatenates lists, negatives replace $a_\ell$ by $-a_\ell$, and right multiplication replaces it by $a_\ell b$. Thus $G(T)$ is a graded right submodule containing $T$ (use $1\in A^0$). Since $d_N(U)\subseteq U\cup\{0\}$ and $d_N(u a)=d_N(u)a+(-1)^{|u|}u d_A(a)$, differentiating a displayed sum produces another such sum in degree $k+1$. Hence $G(T)$ is a DG submodule.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: If $T$ is countable, then $U=T\cup d_N(T)$ is countable by the image observation and the binary-union clause of [lem-trf-countable-unions]. The alphabet $U\times\coprod_i A^i$ is countable by the product coding and the hypothesis on $A$. Its finite lists are countable by [lem-sfb-countable-finite-lists]. For each degree $k$, the lists satisfying the degree condition in the preceding step form a subset, and summation maps this subset onto $G(T)^k$, so that $G(T)^k$ is countable. Apply the countable-family union clause of [lem-trf-countable-unions] to the subsets $\{k\}\times G(T)^k$ of $\coprod_i N^i$, indexed by the countable set $\mathbf Z$: the entire homogeneous set of $G(T)$ is countable. In particular the degree-labelled zeros from empty lists cause no exception.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: For every $i\in\mathbf Z$ and $h\in H^i(N)$ choose a cycle $z_{i,h}\in N^i$ representing $h$, using the surjection $\ker d_N^i\to H^i(N)$ in the definition of cohomology. For fixed $i$ its chosen representatives form a countable image of the countable group $H^i(N)$. The degree-labelled union $S=\{z_{i,h}\}_{i,h}$ is countable by [lem-trf-countable-unions] and the coding observations. Set $M_0=G(S)$. The two preceding steps make $M_0$ a countable DG submodule of $N$. Each $z_{i,h}$ remains a cycle in $M_0$, so $H^i(M_0)\to H^i(N)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: Inductively suppose $M_n\subseteq N$ is a DG submodule with countable homogeneous set. Let $B_n$ be the subset of homogeneous elements $b\in M_n^i$ such that $d_N b=0$ and $b=d_N y$ for some $y\in N^{i-1}$. It is countable as a subset of the homogeneous set of $M_n$. For each such degree-labelled $b$ choose one $y_b\in N^{i-1}$ with $d_N y_b=b$. The homogeneous set $P_n=\{y_b:b\in B_n\}$ is countable by the image observation. The union $T_n=(\coprod_i M_n^i)\cup P_n$, regarded inside $\coprod_i N^i$, is countable by [lem-trf-countable-unions]. Define $M_{n+1}=G(T_n)$. Steps 2–3 prove the induction claim and give $M_n\subseteq M_{n+1}$. Every cycle of $M_n$ which is a boundary in $N$ is now a boundary in $M_{n+1}$, because its chosen primitive lies there.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: Set $M^i=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbf N}M_n^i$ inside $N^i$. Two elements of $M^i$ lie together in $M_{\max(n,m)}^i$, so their sum and negatives lie in $M^i$; multiplication by a homogeneous element of $A$ and the differential preserve the union because they preserve every stage. Thus $M$ is a graded right DG submodule of $N$. Its homogeneous set is $\bigcup_n\coprod_i M_n^i$, a countable union of countable subsets of $\coprod_i N^i$, hence countable by [lem-trf-countable-unions].

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), paragraph beginning Assume A is countable: countable module representative, by the same adjoining-primitives argument as the preceding subalgebra construction.

proof.text: The inclusion $M\hookrightarrow N$ induces a surjection on $H^i$ because all the chosen cycles $z_{i,h}$ already lie in $M_0$. For injectivity, take a cycle $b\in M^i$ whose class vanishes in $H^i(N)$. Choose $n$ with $b\in M_n^i$. Vanishing means exactly $b=d_N y$ for some $y\in N^{i-1}$, so $b\in B_n$. Its chosen primitive $y_b$ lies in $M_{n+1}^{i-1}\subseteq M^{i-1}$ and satisfies $d_M y_b=b$. Hence $[b]=0$ in $H^i(M)$. All cohomology maps are bijective homomorphisms and therefore isomorphisms, which is the stated definition of quasi-isomorphism.
